query: How do review themes differ between positive and negative Yelp sentiment?

per_column.name: service_staff_behavior
per_column.rationale: Captures a distinct review theme (staff conduct) with well-separated, interpretable categories (friendly, rude, indifferent) that can be segmented and cross-tabulated against label_pos to reveal how service themes differ by sentiment.

per_column.name: food_quality_signal
per_column.rationale: An external thematic axis on food quality with an ordered, interpretable scale (excellent to inedible). Distinct from the sentiment label itself and directly groupable for comparison against positive/negative reviews.

per_column.name: food_freshness_issue
per_column.rationale: A more specific theme (freshness/hygiene) with interpretable categories. Some categories are sparse (4 each), but the dominant fresh vs. issue split still supports meaningful segmentation against sentiment.

per_column.name: return_intent
per_column.rationale: Captures reviewer's stated return intention as an interpretable ordinal category. Highly associated with but not identical to sentiment; it is a downstream behavioral theme worth comparing, though it borders on restating overall satisfaction.

judge.rationale: All four added columns are external, thematic categorical variables with interpretable, well-separated categories that can be grouped and cross-tabulated against the focus (label_pos), directly serving the query about how review themes differ by sentiment. They avoid opaque scores and mere restatements of the focus (return_intent leans closest to restating sentiment but adds a distinct behavioral angle). Weaknesses: high NULL/not-assessed/neutral dominance in each column reduces effective comparison mass, and freshness sub-categories are very sparse, slightly limiting the strength of relationships discoverable. Overall a strong, interpretable segmentation set for EDA.
